Subject: Unattributed token spike overnight (EU) / VAT handling?

Hi Mina,

We noticed a ~37k token increase in our EU usage window last night (between 23:45 UTC and 01:10 UTC) that doesn't map to any of our known jobs. The charge hit our July invoice as a single unattributed line item. Attached is a small sample export (usage_sample_20280717.csv) and a screenshot of the billed line (billing_window_screenshot.png).

Two quick asks: 1) Can Redwood help allocate those tokens to a tenant/instance? 2) From a tax perspective, should this be treated as part of our EU entity usage (reverse-charge) or handled as an unexpected surcharge?

We are in the middle of month-end reconciliation, so any provisional guidance would be very helpful.

Thanks,

Hi Elena — thanks for the heads up and for attaching the samples. I'm looping in Ben (billing) and Kimberly (tax) so we can triage allocation and VAT treatment in parallel.

Initial notes from a quick glance:
- The sample shows requests routed to an aux model pool around 23:58 UTC; those are often short-lived prefetched requests.
- Unattributed lines like this can be caused by prefetched/standby traffic that never got associated to a tenant id due to a routing fallback — we have a couple of telemetry checks that can catch that.

Can you confirm: BrightLoop's EU billed entity is "BrightLoop Ltd (GB/EU)" and the billing identifier on file is BL-ENT-004? If yes, we'll proceed with a ledger trace for that 23:45–01:10 window and propose a provisional credit workflow if we confirm orphaned tokens.

Ben — can you pull the session traces and the requestid footprint for BL-ENT-004 for the timeframe? Kimberly, if we confirm orphaned tokens in EU, do you recommend treating the provisional credit as a non-taxable adjustment or do we need to issue a corrected invoice for VAT reporting?

I'll follow up within 24 hours with the initial trace results.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Mina/Elena—I'm on it. Quick update on next steps:

1) I've kicked off a ledger trace (BILL-4021) for BL-ENT-004 covering 2028-07-17T23:30:00Z to 2028-07-18T01:30:00Z. Expect raw requestid mapping in ~6 hours.
2) If the trace shows requests that hit an aux routing pool without tenant attribution, our standard practice is to grant a provisional credit equal to the unattributed token cost while we finish the forensic. This credit is applied to the next invoice unless otherwise requested.
3) Finance has paused collection on the disputed line while we investigate — I opened internal ticket BILL-4021 and linked the Drive evidence Mina shared.

Kimberly — tagging you for tax treatment guidance. If we issue a provisional credit after the invoice has closed, do we treat that as a VAT-correcting credit note (documented) or a non-taxable adjustment per our EU policy?

Elena — can you confirm the exact legal entity name and VAT number (if available) so we can ensure our ledger attribution is correct? Also, if you have any service tokens/runner IDs that were active in that window, please forward — that speeds the mapping.

Thanks — I'll post the trace dump here as soon as it completes.
